claims.statement: Demeter is an Olympian goddess of harvest, agriculture, and earth's fertility.
claims.statement_id: Demeter adalah dewi Olimpus yang membawahi panen, pertanian, dan kesuburan tanah.
claims.quote: is the Olympian goddess of the harvest and agriculture, presiding over crops, grains, food, and the fertility of the earth.

claims.statement: Demeter is shown as a mature woman bearing wheat or a torch.
claims.statement_id: Demeter digambarkan sebagai perempuan dewasa yang membawa gandum atau obor.
claims.quote: Demeter was depicted as a mature woman, often wearing a crown and bearing sheafs of wheat or a cornucopia (horn of plenty), and a torch.

claims.statement: Persephone is Demeter's daughter abducted by Hades, followed by famine.
claims.statement_id: Persephone adalah putri Demeter yang diculik Hades, diikuti masa kekurangan pangan.
claims.quote: The abduction of her daughter Persephone by Hades, and the great dearth she brought down upon the earth.

claims.statement: Demeter caused a drought to demand Persephone's release.
claims.statement_id: Demeter menyebabkan kekeringan untuk menuntut pembebasan Persephone.
claims.quote: Once the temple was completed, Demeter withdrew from the world and lived inside it; at the same time, she created a great drought to convince the other gods to release Persephone from Hades.

claims.statement: Eleusis had a sanctuary for Demeter and Persephone and their mysteries.
claims.statement_id: Eleusis memiliki tempat suci Demeter dan Persephone serta ritual misteri mereka.
claims.quote: The sanctuary at Eleusis is dedicated to both the goddess and her daughter Persephone. This was the location of the famous Eleusinian Mysteries.

claims.statement: Romans knew Demeter as Ceres.
claims.statement_id: Bangsa Romawi mengenal Demeter sebagai Ceres.
claims.quote: To the Romans, the goddess remained popular and was known as Ceres.

claims.statement: The drought in Demeter's story withered crops.
claims.statement_id: Kekeringan dalam kisah Demeter membuat tanaman layu.
claims.quote: As the drought claimed ever more victims, crops withered

claims.statement: Demeter is a deity in the ancient Greek pantheon.
claims.statement_id: Demeter adalah dewi dalam panteon Yunani kuno.
claims.quote: Demeter was one of the oldest gods in the ancient Greek pantheon.

claims.statement: Some consider the name Demeter the same as "gê mêtêr" (mother earth), while others link "Deo" to the Cretan word for barley, so that Demeter would be the mother or giver of barley or of food generally.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang menganggap nama Demeter sama dengan "gê mêtêr" (ibu bumi); yang lain menghubungkan "Deo" dengan kata Kreta untuk jelai, sehingga Demeter berarti ibu atau pemberi jelai atau makanan pada umumnya.
claims.quote: that is, mother earth, while others consider Deo, which is synonymous with Demeter, as connected with dais and dainumi, and as derived from the Cretan word ... barley, so that Demeter would be the mother or giver of barley or of food generally.

claims.statement: Demeter was the goddess of the earth, and more especially of the earth as producing fruit, and consequently of agriculture.
claims.statement_id: Demeter adalah dewi bumi, terutama bumi yang menghasilkan buah, dan karena itu dewi pertanian.
claims.quote: Demeter was the goddess of the earth (Eurip. Bacch. 276), and more especially of the earth as producing fruit, and consequently of agriculture

claims.statement: Her role in the earth's fertility was extended to fertility in general; she was also regarded as the goddess of marriage and was worshipped especially by women.
claims.statement_id: Anggapan bahwa Demeter menyuburkan bumi diperluas menjadi kesuburan pada umumnya; ia juga dipandang sebagai dewi pernikahan dan dipuja terutama oleh perempuan.
claims.quote: she accordingly was looked upon also as the goddess of marriage (Serv. ad Aen. iv. 58), and was worshipped especially by women.

claims.statement: In her story, Demeter dwelt among men, conferring presents and blessings wherever she was kindly received and severely punishing those who repulsed her or did not receive her gifts with proper reverence.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisahnya, Demeter tinggal di antara manusia, memberi hadiah dan berkat kepada yang menyambutnya dengan baik, dan menghukum dengan keras mereka yang menolaknya atau tidak menerima pemberiannya dengan hormat.
claims.quote: dwelt upon earth among men, conferring presents and blessings wherever she was kindly received, and severely punishing those who repulsed her or did not receive her gifts with proper reverence.

claims.statement: She was represented sometimes sitting, sometimes walking, and sometimes riding in a chariot drawn by horses or dragons, but always in full attire.
claims.statement_id: Demeter digambarkan kadang duduk, kadang berjalan, dan kadang naik kereta yang ditarik kuda atau naga, selalu berpakaian lengkap.
claims.quote: She was represented sometimes in a sitting attitude, sometimes walking, and sometimes riding in a chariot drawn by horses or dragons, but always in full attire.

claims.statement: Sacrifices offered to her consisted of pigs, the symbol of fertility, bulls, cows, honey-cakes, and fruits.
claims.statement_id: Kurban untuknya berupa babi sebagai lambang kesuburan, sapi jantan, sapi betina, kue madu, dan buah-buahan.
claims.quote: The sacrifices offered to her consisted of pigs, the symbol of fertility, bulls, cows, honey-cakes, and fruits.

claims.statement: The spot where Persephone was believed to have been carried into the lower world differs between traditions; the common story places it in Sicily.
claims.statement_id: Tempat Persephone dipercaya dibawa ke dunia bawah berbeda-beda menurut tradisi; kisah yang paling umum menempatkannya di Sisilia.
claims.quote: The spot where Persephone was believed to have been carried into the lower world is different in the different traditions; the common story places it in Sicily

claims.statement: Her home is Mount Olympus; her symbols are the sheaf of grain and cornucopia; her sacred animals are the snake and pig; her sacred plants are wheat, mint, and poppy.
claims.statement_id: Tempat tinggalnya Gunung Olimpus; lambangnya berkas gandum dan cornucopia; hewan sucinya ular dan babi; tumbuhan sucinya gandum, mint, dan opium poppy.
claims.quote: Home Mount Olympus Symbols Sheaf of grain, cornucopia Sacred Animals Snake, pig Sacred Plants Wheat, mint, poppy

claims.statement: Erysichthon was cursed by the goddess with an unquenchable hunger for cutting down her holy grove.
claims.statement_id: Erysichthon dikutuk dengan rasa lapar yang tak terpuaskan oleh sang dewi karena menebang hutan sucinya.
claims.quote: The punishment of Erysikhthon (Erysichthon) who was cursed with an unquenchable hunger by the goddess for cutting down her holy grove.

claims.statement: Triptolemos was a hero sent by the goddess to instruct mankind in agriculture.
claims.statement_id: Triptolemos adalah pahlawan yang diutus sang dewi untuk mengajarkan pertanian kepada manusia.
claims.quote: The journeys of Triptolemos, a hero sent by the goddess to instruct mankind in agriculture.

claims.statement: Demeter was the daughter of Kronos and Rhea, sister of Zeus, Poseidon, Hades, Hera, and Hestia, and mother of Persephone and Iacchus (both with Zeus) and Plutus, the god of wealth.
claims.statement_id: Demeter adalah putri Kronos dan Rhea, saudari Zeus, Poseidon, Hades, Hera, dan Hestia, serta ibu Persephone dan Iacchus (keduanya dengan Zeus) dan Plutus, dewa kekayaan.
claims.quote: Daughter of Kronos and Rhea, sister of Zeus, Poseidon, Hades, Hera, and Hestia, Demeter was the mother of Persephone and Iacchus (both with Zeus) and Plutus, the god of wealth

claims.statement: To escape Poseidon, Demeter changed into a mare; Poseidon too changed into a horse and their offspring was Arion, the winged horse ridden by Hercules.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menghindari Poseidon, Demeter berubah menjadi kuda betina; Poseidon pun berubah menjadi kuda dan keturunan mereka adalah Arion, kuda bersayap yang ditunggangi Hercules.
claims.quote: Demeter was also pursued by Poseidon, and to escape his attentions, she changed into a mare; however, Poseidon too changed into a horse and their resulting offspring was Arion, the winged horse ridden by Hercules.

claims.statement: At Eleusis, disguised as an old woman, the goddess cared for Demophon (or Triptolemus), the only son of Metaneira, wife of Keleos (or Celeus), king of Eleusis.
claims.statement_id: Di Eleusis, menyamar sebagai perempuan tua, sang dewi merawat Demophon (atau Triptolemus), putra tunggal Metaneira, istri Keleos (atau Celeus), raja Eleusis.
claims.quote: It was here, disguised as an old woman, that the goddess cared for Demophon (or Triptolemus), the only son of Metaneira, the wife of Keleos (or Celeus), king of Eleusis.

claims.statement: As a compromise, Persephone would be released but had to return to Hades for one-third of the year (or one half in other accounts).
claims.statement_id: Sebagai kompromi, Persephone dibebaskan tetapi harus kembali kepada Hades selama sepertiga tahun (atau separuh tahun dalam kisah lain).
claims.quote: Finally, as a compromise, it was decided that Persephone would be released but that she would have to return to Hades for one-third of the year (or in other accounts one half).

claims.statement: The story of Demeter and Persephone was perhaps symbolic of the changing seasons and the cycle from life to death to life once more, from summer to winter and the return of life in spring.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Demeter dan Persephone mungkin melambangkan pergantian musim dan siklus dari hidup ke kematian lalu hidup kembali, yakni dari musim panas ke musim dingin dan kembalinya kehidupan di musim semi.
claims.quote: The story of Demeter and Persephone was perhaps symbolic of the changing seasons and the perennial change from life to death, to life once more, or, in other words, the changes from summer to winter and the return of life in spring.

claims.statement: From c. 600 BCE the Eleusinian Mysteries became an official ceremony in the Athenian calendar.
claims.statement_id: Sejak sekitar 600 SM, Misteri Eleusis menjadi upacara resmi dalam kalender Athena.
claims.quote: From c. 600 BCE the Eleusinian Mysteries became an official ceremony in the Athenian calendar

claims.statement: Closely associated with fertility and agriculture, the mysteries probably brought worshippers good fortune and, most importantly for most participants, the promise of a better afterlife.
claims.statement_id: Misteri yang erat kaitannya dengan kesuburan dan pertanian itu kemungkinan memberi peserta keberuntungan dan, yang terpenting bagi kebanyakan mereka, janji kehidupan akhirat yang lebih baik.
claims.quote: Closely associated with fertility and agriculture, the mysteries probably brought worshippers good fortune and, perhaps most important for most participants, the promise of a better afterlife.

claims.statement: In Archaic and Classical art she is often seated, wears a crown of grain and holds a torch (signifying her search for her lost daughter) or a sceptre, a poppy, or simply stalks of grain.
claims.statement_id: Dalam seni Arkais dan Klasik, Demeter sering duduk, bermahkota biji-bijian, dan memegang obor (tanda pencariannya akan putrinya), tongkat kerajaan, opium poppy, atau sekadar tangkai gandum.
claims.quote: In Archaic and Classical art she is often seated, wears a crown of grain and holds a torch (signifying her search for her lost daughter) or a sceptre, a poppy (the flower that grows so abundantly in untended wheat fields) or simply stalks of grain.

claims.statement: The Thesmophoria was an all-female autumn festival in Attica to honour Demeter.
claims.statement_id: Thesmophoria adalah festival musim gugur khusus perempuan di Attika untuk menghormati Demeter.
claims.quote: The Thesmophoria, meanwhile, was an all-female autumn festival in Attica to honour Demeter.

claims.statement: Demeter was probably a reincarnation of local mother Earth goddesses worshipped in rural communities in Bronze Age Greece.
claims.statement_id: Demeter kemungkinan merupakan penjelmaan kembali dewi-dewi ibu bumi setempat yang dipuja masyarakat pedesaan di Yunani Zaman Perunggu.
claims.quote: Demeter was probably a reincarnation of local mother Earth goddesses worshipped in rural communities in Bronze Age Greece.

claims.statement: In the Homeric Hymn, Demeter caused a most dreadful and cruel year for mankind: the ground would not make the seed sprout, for Demeter kept it hid.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Himne Homerik, Demeter menyebabkan tahun yang sangat mengerikan bagi manusia: tanah tidak menumbuhkan benih karena Demeter menyembunyikannya.
claims.quote: Then she caused a most dreadful and cruel year for mankind over the all-nourishing earth: the ground would not make the seed sprout, for rich-crowned Demeter kept it hid.

claims.statement: Demeter would have made the child in her care deathless and unageing, but Metaneira kept watch by night and spied.
claims.statement_id: Demeter hampir membuat anak asuhannya tak mati dan tak menua, tetapi gagal karena Metaneira mengintip pada malam hari.
claims.quote: And she would have made him deathless and unageing, had not well-girded Metaneira in her heedlessness kept watch by night from her sweet-smelling chamber and spied.

claims.statement: Once persuaded, Demeter straightway made fruit spring up from the rich lands so that the whole wide earth was laden with leaves and flowers.
claims.statement_id: Setelah dibujuk, Demeter segera menumbuhkan buah dari tanah subur sehingga seluruh bumi dipenuhi daun dan bunga.
claims.quote: did not refuse but straightway made fruit to spring up from the rich lands, so that the whole wide earth was laden with leaves and flowers.

claims.statement: Demeter showed the conduct of her rites and taught her mysteries to Triptolemus, Polyxeinus, and Diocles.
claims.statement_id: Demeter menunjukkan tata cara ritusnya dan mengajarkan seluruh misterinya kepada Triptolemus, Polyxeinus, dan Diocles.
claims.quote: she showed the conduct of her rites and taught them all her mysteries, to Triptolemus and Polyxeinus and Diocles also

claims.statement: Demeter declares she has a share of honour and is the greatest help and cause of joy to the undying gods and mortal men.
claims.statement_id: Demeter menyatakan dirinya mendapat bagian kehormatan dan menjadi penolong terbesar serta sebab sukacita bagi para dewa dan manusia.
claims.quote: Lo! I am that Demeter who has share of honour and is the greatest help and cause of joy to the undying gods and mortal men.

claims.statement: The goddess changed her stature and her looks, thrusting old age away, so that beauty spread around her and a lovely fragrance was wafted from her robes.
claims.statement_id: Demeter mengubah perawakan dan rupanya, menyingkirkan ketuaan, sehingga keindahan menyebar di sekitarnya dan keharuman tercium dari jubahnya.
claims.quote: the goddess changed her stature and her looks, thrusting old age away from her: beauty spread round about her and a lovely fragrance was wafted from her sweet-smelling robes

claims.statement: In the Homeric Hymn, the earth yawned in the plain of Nysa and the lord, the Host of Many, sprang out with his immortal horses.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Himne Homerik, bumi terbelah di dataran Nysa dan sang penguasa, Tuan Banyak Tamu (Host of Many), melompat keluar dengan kuda-kuda abadinya.
claims.quote: the wide-pathed earth yawned there in the plain of Nysa, and the lord, Host of Many, with his immortal horses sprang out upon her

claims.statement: Zeus agreed that her daughter should go down to darkness for the third part of the circling year and live with her mother and the other gods for the two parts.
claims.statement_id: Zeus menyetujui bahwa putri Demeter turun ke kegelapan selama sepertiga tahun dan tinggal bersama ibunya dan dewa-dewa lain selama dua pertiga tahun.
claims.quote: agreed that her daughter should go down for the third part of the circling year to darkness and gloom, but for the two parts should live with her mother and the other deathless gods.

claims.statement: Dionysus is a Greek deity associated with wine, vegetation, and festivities.
claims.statement_id: Dionysus adalah dewa Yunani yang berkaitan dengan anggur, tumbuhan, dan perayaan.
claims.quote: is the god of wine-making, orchards, fruit, vegetation, fertility, festivity, insanity, ritual madness, religious ecstasy, and theatre.

claims.statement: Dionysus is known as the Greek god of wine, merriment, and theatre.
claims.statement_id: Dionysus dikenal sebagai dewa Yunani bagi anggur, kegembiraan, dan teater.
claims.quote: was the ancient Greek god of wine, merriment, and theatre.

claims.statement: Dionysus is an Olympian god of wine, vegetation, and festivity.
claims.statement_id: Dionysus adalah dewa Olimpus yang berhubungan dengan anggur, tumbuhan, dan perayaan.
claims.quote: DIONYSOS (Dionysus) was the Olympian god of wine, vegetation, pleasure, festivity, madness and wild frenzy.

claims.statement: Dionysus is depicted as a bearded man or long-haired youth with a thyrsos and ivy.
claims.statement_id: Dionysus digambarkan sebagai lelaki berjanggut atau pemuda berambut panjang dengan thyrsos dan ivy.
claims.quote: He was depicted as either an older, bearded god or an effeminate, long-haired youth. His attributes included the thyrsos (a pine-cone tipped staff), a drinking cup and a crown of ivy.

claims.statement: Dionysus is a son of Zeus and Semele.
claims.statement_id: Dionysus adalah putra Zeus dan Semele.
claims.quote: Dionysos was a son of Zeus and the princess Semele of Thebes.

claims.statement: After Semele died Zeus carried the unborn child in his thigh.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Semele meninggal, Zeus membawa anak yang belum lahir di pahanya.
claims.quote: This was too much for the mortal and she immediately expired; however, Zeus took the unborn child and reared him in his thigh.

claims.statement: Bacchus is the Roman name for Dionysus.
claims.statement_id: Bacchus adalah nama Dionysus dalam tradisi Romawi.
claims.quote: Dionysos (Roman name: Bacchus, also known as Dionysus)

claims.statement: Greeks and Romans also called him Bacchus (Bakchos), that is, the noisy or riotous god.
claims.statement_id: Greek dan Romawi juga menyebutnya Bacchus (Bakchos), yang berarti dewa yang gaduh atau liar.
claims.quote: He is also called both by Greeks and Romans Bacchus (Bakchos), that is, the noisy or riotous god

claims.statement: According to the common tradition Dionysus was the son of Zeus and Semele, daughter of Cadmus of Thebes; others describe him as a son of Zeus by Demeter, Io, Dione, or Arge.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi umum, Dionysus putra Zeus dan Semele, putri Kadmos dari Thebes; yang lain menyebutnya putra Zeus dengan Demeter, Io, Dione, atau Arge.
claims.quote: According to the common tradition, Dionysus was the son of Zeus and Semele, the daughter of Cadmus of Thebes ... whereas others describe him as a son of Zeus by Demeter, Io, Dione, or Arge.

claims.statement: In the common tradition his native place is Thebes, while others name India, Libya, Crete, Dracanum in Samos, Naxos, Elis, Eleutherae, or Teos as his birthplace.
claims.statement_id: Tempat kelahirannya menurut tradisi umum adalah Thebes, sedangkan tradisi lain menyebut India, Libya, Kreta, Dracanum di Samos, Naxos, Elis, Eleutherae, atau Teos.
claims.quote: while in others we find India, Libya, Crete, Dracanum in Samos, Naxos, Elis, Eleutherae, or Teos, mentioned as his birthplace

claims.statement: When Dionysus had grown up, Hera threw him into a state of madness in which he wandered through many countries of the earth.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Dionysus dewasa, Hera membuatnya gila sehingga ia mengembara ke banyak negeri.
claims.quote: When Dionysus had grown up, Hera threw him also into a state of madness, in which he wandered about through many countries of the earth.

claims.statement: Dionysus with the host of Pans, Satyrs, and Bacchic women conquered his enemies and taught the Indians the cultivation of the vine and of various fruits, and the worship of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Dionysus bersama rombongan Pan, satir, dan perempuan Bacchus menaklukkan musuh-musuhnya dan mengajarkan kepada orang India budi daya anggur dan berbagai buah serta pemujaan dewa-dewa.
claims.quote: But Dionysus and the host of Pans, Satyrs, and Bacchic women, by whom he was accompanied, conquered his enemies, taught the Indians the cultivation of the vine and of various fruits, and the worship of the gods

claims.statement: After Lycurgus took Dionysus's host prisoner, the country of the Edones ceased to bear fruit and Lycurgus became mad and killed his own son, whom he mistook for a vine.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Lycurgus menawan rombongan Dionysus, negeri bangsa Edones berhenti berbuah dan Lycurgus menjadi gila serta membunuh putranya sendiri yang ia kira pohon anggur.
claims.quote: The country of the Edones thereupon ceased to bear fruit, and Lycurgus became mad and killed his own son, whom he mistook for a vine

claims.statement: Pentheus, who ruled at Thebes, tried to check the Bacchic proceedings and went out to the mountains; his own mother, Agave, in her Bacchic fury, mistook him for an animal and tore him to pieces.
claims.statement_id: Pentheus, penguasa Thebes, berusaha menghentikan perayaan Bacchus dan pergi ke pegunungan; ibunya sendiri, Agave, dalam kegilaan Bacchus mengiranya hewan dan mencabik-cabiknya.
claims.quote: Pentheus, who then ruled at Thebes, endeavoured to check the riotous proceedings, and went out to the mountains to seek the Bacchic women; but his own mother, Agave, in her Bacchic fury, mistook him for an animal, and tore him to pieces.

claims.statement: On perceiving the pirates' plan, the god changed the mast and oars into serpents and himself into a lion; he filled the vessel with ivy and the sound of flutes, so that the sailors, seized with madness, leaped into the sea and were metamorphosed into dolphins.
claims.statement_id: Ketika menyadari niat para bajak laut, Dionysus mengubah tiang dan dayung menjadi ular dan dirinya menjadi singa; kapal dipenuhi ivy dan bunyi seruling sehingga para pelaut menjadi gila, melompat ke laut, dan menjadi lumba-lumba.
claims.quote: The god, however, on perceiving this, changed the mast and oars into serpents, and himself into a lion; he filled the vessel with ivy and the sound of flutes, so that the sailors, who were seized with madness, leaped into the sea, where they were metamorphosed into dolphins.

claims.statement: Dionysus is the god of wine, the inventor and teacher of its cultivation, the giver of joy, and the disperser of grief and sorrow.
claims.statement_id: Dionysus adalah dewa anggur, penemu dan pengajar budi dayanya, pemberi kegembiraan, dan penghalau duka.
claims.quote: Dionysus is, therefore, the god of wine, the inventor and teacher of its cultivation, the giver of joy, and the disperser of grief and sorrow.

claims.statement: As the god of wine he is also an inspired and an inspiring god, that is, a god with the power of revealing the future to man by oracles.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai dewa anggur, Dionysus juga dewa yang terilhami dan mengilhami, yaitu memiliki kuasa menyingkapkan masa depan kepada manusia lewat orakel.
claims.quote: As the god of wine, he is also both an inspired and an inspiring god, that is, a god who has the power of revealing the future to man by oracles.

claims.statement: At his oracle of Amphicleia, in Phocis, he cured diseases by revealing the remedies to the sufferers in their dreams.
claims.statement_id: Di orakelnya di Amphicleia, Phocis, Dionysus menyembuhkan penyakit dengan menyingkapkan obat kepada para penderita dalam mimpi mereka.
claims.quote: at his oracle of Amphicleia, in Phocis, he cured diseases by revealing the remedies to the sufferers in their dreams.

claims.statement: As Greek drama grew out of the dithyrambic choruses at the festivals of Dionysus, he was also regarded as the god of tragic art and the protector of theatres.
claims.statement_id: Karena drama Yunani tumbuh dari paduan suara dithyramb pada festival Dionysus, ia juga dipandang sebagai dewa seni tragedi dan pelindung teater.
claims.quote: As the Greek drama had grown out of the dithyrambic choruses at the festivals of Dionysus, he was also regarded as the god of tragic art, and as the protector of theatres.

claims.statement: Sileni, Pans, satyrs, centaurs, and other beings of a like kind are the constant companions of the god.
claims.statement_id: Sileni, Pan, satir, centaur, dan makhluk sejenisnya adalah pendamping tetap sang dewa.
claims.quote: Sileni, Pans, satyrs, centaurs, and other beings of a like kind, are also the constant companions of the god.

claims.statement: Things sacred to him include the vine, ivy, laurel, and asphodel; the dolphin, serpent, tiger, lynx, panther, and ass; but he hated the sight of an owl.
claims.statement_id: Hal-hal yang suci baginya antara lain pohon anggur, ivy, laurel, dan asphodel; lumba-lumba, ular, harimau, lynx, macan tutul, dan keledai; tetapi ia membenci pemandangan burung hantu.
claims.quote: Among the things sacred to him, we may notice the vine, ivy, laurel, and asphodel; the dolphin, serpent, tiger, lynx, panther, and ass; but he hated the sight of an owl.

claims.statement: The animal most commonly sacrificed to Dionysus was a ram.
claims.statement_id: Hewan yang paling sering dikurbankan bagi Dionysus adalah domba jantan.
claims.quote: The animal most commonly sacrificed to Dionysus was a ram.

claims.statement: Dionysus led his mother out of Hades, called her Thyone, and rose with her into Olympus.
claims.statement_id: Dionysus menuntun ibunya keluar dari Hades, menamainya Thyone, dan naik bersamanya ke Olimpus.
claims.quote: he led his mother out of Hades, called her Thyone, and rose with her into Olympus.

claims.statement: There is also a mystical story that the body of Dionysus was cut up and thrown into a cauldron by the Titans, and that he was restored and cured by Rhea or Demeter.
claims.statement_id: Ada kisah mistik bahwa tubuh Dionysus dicincang dan dilemparkan ke dalam kuali oleh para Titan, lalu dipulihkan dan disembuhkan oleh Rhea atau Demeter.
claims.quote: There is also a mystical story, that the body of Dionysus was cut up and thrown into a cauldron by the Titans, and that he was restored and cured by Rhea or Demeter.

claims.statement: In the Homeric poems Dionysus does not appear as one of the great divinities, but is simply described as the god who teaches man the preparation of wine.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi-puisi Homeros, Dionysus tidak tampil sebagai salah satu dewa besar, dan ceritanya hanya digambarkan sebagai dewa yang mengajarkan manusia membuat anggur.
claims.quote: in those poems Dionysus does not appear as one of the great divinities, and the story of his birth by Zeus and the Bacchic orgies are not alluded to in any way : Dionysus is there simply described as the god who teaches man the preparation of wine

claims.statement: The god gave Ikarios, a noble citizen of Ikaria in Attica, the vine tree.
claims.statement_id: Sang dewa memberikan pohon anggur kepada Ikarios, warga terhormat Ikaria di Attika.
claims.quote: The god gave Ikarios, a noble citizen of Ikaria in Attica, the vine tree.

claims.statement: In gratitude, the god granted Midas a wish; the king asked that everything he touched turn to gold, and almost died of starvation and thirst until Dionysos reversed the gift by telling him to wash in the Pactolus river.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai balas budi, sang dewa mengabulkan satu permintaan Midas; raja meminta semua yang disentuhnya menjadi emas, hingga hampir mati kelaparan dan kehausan, sampai Dionysos membatalkan pemberian itu dengan menyuruhnya mandi di sungai Pactolus.
claims.quote: In gratitude, the god granted Midas a wish. The king requested that everything he touched would turn to gold but alas this included food and water, so the king almost died of starvation and thirst until Dionysos reversed the gift by telling Midas to wash in the Pactolus river.

claims.statement: The god transformed the ship's mast into a huge vine, the sails dripped with wine, and a heavenly choir filled the air with music; Dionysos transformed himself into a lion and, assisted by a bear, dispatched the pirate captain.
claims.statement_id: Sang dewa mengubah tiang kapal menjadi pohon anggur raksasa, layar meneteskan anggur, dan paduan suara surgawi memenuhi udara; Dionysos berubah menjadi singa dan, dibantu seekor beruang, menghabisi kapten bajak laut.
claims.quote: The god transformed the ship's mast into a huge vine, the sails dripped with wine, and a heavenly choir filled the air with music. Dionysos transformed himself into a lion and, assisted by a bear, he dispatched the pirate captain.

claims.statement: At Naxos, Dionysos fell in love with and married Ariadne when Theseus stopped off on his return from killing the Minotaur.
claims.statement_id: Di Naxos, Dionysos jatuh cinta dan menikahi Ariadne ketika Theseus singgah dalam perjalanan pulang setelah membunuh Minotaur.
claims.quote: falling in love with and marrying Ariadne when Theseus stopped off on his return from killing the Minotaur.

claims.statement: In her gratitude Hera ensured that Dionysos, actually only a demigod, became a full Olympian god with permission to reside on Mt. Olympus for all time.
claims.statement_id: Dalam rasa terima kasih, Hera memastikan Dionysos, yang sebenarnya hanya setengah dewa, menjadi dewa Olimpus penuh dengan izin tinggal di Gunung Olimpus selamanya.
claims.quote: Hera in her gratitude ensured that Dionysos, actually only a demigod, became a full Olympian god with permission to reside on Mt. Olympus for all time.

claims.statement: Lycurgus, King of Thrace, and Pentheus, King of Thebes, both suffered Dionysos' wrath when they tried to stop the excesses of his festivals; the former was driven mad and the latter was ripped to pieces by a maddened group of female worshippers.
claims.statement_id: Lycurgus, raja Thrace, dan Pentheus, raja Thebes, sama-sama menanggung murka Dionysos ketika mencoba menghentikan perayaannya; yang pertama menjadi gila dan yang kedua dicabik oleh para pemuja perempuan yang kalap.
claims.quote: Lycurgus, King of Thrace, and Pentheus, King of Thebes, both suffered Dionysos' wrath when they prudishly tried to stop the excesses of the god's festivals. The former was driven mad and the latter was ripped to pieces by a maddened group of female worshippers after he had disguised himself as a woman to spy on their debauchery.

claims.statement: The cult of Dionysos became a significant part of Greek religion in Athens from the 6th century BCE, and the Dionysia festival would later evolve into the Bacchanalia of Rome.
claims.statement_id: Kultus Dionysos menjadi bagian penting agama Yunani di Athena sejak abad ke-6 SM, dan festival Dionysia kemudian berkembang menjadi Bacchanalia di Roma.
claims.quote: The cult of Dionysos became a significant part of the Greek religion in Athens from the 6th century BCE and the Dionysia festival of Athens and other cities would later evolve into the Bacchanalia of Rome.

claims.statement: The island of Naxos was a particularly important sanctuary to the god; there is evidence of a cult of Dionysos dating from the Mycenaean period (14th century BCE).
claims.statement_id: Pulau Naxos adalah tempat suci yang sangat penting bagi sang dewa; ada bukti kultus Dionysos sejak masa Mikenai (abad ke-14 SM).
claims.quote: The island of Naxos was a particularly important sanctuary to the god. There is evidence of a cult to Dionysos dating from the Mycenaean period (14th century BCE)

claims.statement: Dionysos is often identified through his association with the vine, thyrsos, a kantharos or drinking-horn, and on occasion a wreath of ivy or the pelt of a panther.
claims.statement_id: Dionysos sering dikenali dari kaitannya dengan pohon anggur, thyrsos, kantharos atau tanduk minum, dan kadang karangan ivy atau kulit macan tutul.
claims.quote: He is often identified through his association with the vine, thyrsos - a sacred rod topped with ivy and vine leaves and sometimes a pinecone, a kantharos - drinking vessel for wine - or a drinking-horn, and on occasion, he wears a wreath of ivy or the pelt of a panther.

claims.statement: In Archaic and Classical Greek art, Dionysos is often depicted with his thiasos or troupe of satyrs and nymphs, who from the late 6th century BCE were replaced by maenads, daemonic creatures who in Dionysian frenzy hunted the forests for victims and ate their raw flesh.
claims.statement_id: Dalam seni Arkais dan Klasik, Dionysos sering digambarkan bersama thiasos, rombongan satir dan nimfa, yang sejak akhir abad ke-6 SM digantikan para maenad, makhluk daimonik yang saat dilanda kegilaan Dionysian memburu korban di hutan dan memakan dagingnya mentah.
claims.quote: is often depicted with his thiasos or troupe of satyrs (half-men, half-goat) and nymphs, who from the late 6th century BCE were replaced by maenads, daemonic creatures, who when overtaken by Dionysian frenzy, hunted the forests for victims and ate their raw flesh.

claims.statement: It is believed that theatre sprang from this activity as actors, like Dionysos' worshippers, strive to leave behind their own persona and become one with the character they play; priests of Dionysos were given seats of honour in Greek theatres.
claims.statement_id: Diyakini teater bermula dari kegiatan ritual ini karena para aktor, seperti pemuja Dionysos, berusaha meninggalkan pribadi mereka dan menyatu dengan tokoh yang dimainkan; para imam Dionysos mendapat tempat duduk kehormatan di teater Yunani.
claims.quote: It is believed that theatre sprang from this activity as, like Dionysos' worshippers, actors strive to leave behind their own persona and become one with the character they are playing. Indeed, priests of Dionysos were given seats of honour in Greek theatres.

claims.statement: Most accounts attribute the satyrs and nymphs as the carers of Dionysos in his childhood and the wise Silenus as his chief educator on Mt. Nysa, far from Hera's wrath.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian besar kisah menyebut para satir dan nimfa sebagai pengasuh Dionysos di masa kecil, dan Silenus yang bijak sebagai pendidik utamanya di Gunung Nysa, jauh dari murka Hera.
claims.quote: Most accounts then attribute the satyrs and nymphs as the carers of Dionysos in his childhood and the wise Silenus as his chief educator on Mt. Nysa, far from Hera's wrath.

claims.statement: In Homeric Hymn 7, the pirates' bonds would not hold him and fell away from his hands and feet.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Himne Homerik VII, ikatan para bajak laut tidak dapat menahannya dan lepas dari tangan dan kakinya.
claims.quote: the bonds would not hold him, and the withes fell far away from his hands and feet

claims.statement: In Homeric Hymn 7, sweet, fragrant wine ran streaming throughout the ship and a heavenly smell arose.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Himne Homerik VII, anggur yang manis dan harum mengalir di seluruh kapal dan aroma surgawi menyebar.
claims.quote: But soon strange things were seen among them. First of all sweet, fragrant wine ran streaming throughout all the black ship and a heavenly smell arose

claims.statement: In Homeric Hymn 7, the god changed into a dreadful lion on the ship; the sailors leapt overboard and were changed into dolphins.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Himne Homerik VII, sang dewa berubah menjadi singa yang mengerikan di kapal; para pelaut melompat ke laut dan berubah menjadi lumba-lumba.
claims.quote: But the god changed into a dreadful lion there on the ship, in the bows, and roared loudly ... and were changed into dolphins.

claims.statement: In Homeric Hymn 26, the rich-haired Nymphs received him from his father and nurtured him carefully in the dells of Nysa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Himne Homerik XXVI, para Nimfa berambut indah menerimanya dari ayahnya dan merawatnya dengan cermat di lembah Nysa.
claims.quote: The rich-haired Nymphs received him in their bosoms from the lord his father and fostered and nurtured him carefully in the dells of Nysa

claims.statement: A mermaid is a mythical sea being with a woman's upper body and a fish tail.
claims.statement_id: Putri duyung adalah makhluk laut mitis berkepala dan bertubuh atas perempuan serta berekor ikan.
claims.quote: A mermaid is a mythical sea-dwelling creature, often described as having the head and body of a woman and a fish's tail below the waist.

claims.statement: Mermaid stories span cultures around the world.
claims.statement_id: Cerita putri duyung tersebar di berbagai budaya dunia.
claims.quote: Stories of mermaids have existed for thousands of years and span cultures across the world

claims.statement: Some traditions link mermaids to sea fertility and others to danger for sailors.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian tradisi mengaitkan putri duyung dengan kesuburan laut, sebagian lain dengan bahaya bagi pelaut.
claims.quote: In some cultures, the mermaid signifies life and fertility within the ocean. In others, she embodies the destructive nature of the water, luring sailors to their deaths

claims.statement: Southeast Asian tales include the mermaid princess Suvannamaccha.
claims.statement_id: Cerita Asia Tenggara mengenal putri duyung Suvannamaccha.
claims.quote: Southeast Asian folklore includes the story of a mermaid princess, Suvannamaccha

claims.statement: Early Greek sirens were woman-bird beings often confused with mermaids.
claims.statement_id: Siren Yunani awal berwujud perempuan dan burung, tetapi kerap tertukar dengan putri duyung.
claims.quote: In early Greek mythology, the sirens were half-women, half-bird creatures and are often confused with mermaids.

claims.statement: Reported dugong sightings have been associated with mermaids.
claims.statement_id: Laporan penampakan dugong pernah dikaitkan dengan putri duyung.
claims.quote: Sightings of dugongs, a member of the manatee’s order, have also been associated with mermaids throughout history.

claims.statement: Folkloric mermaids have a woman's upper body and fish tail.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat putri duyung memiliki tubuh atas perempuan dan ekor ikan.
claims.quote: In folklore, a mermaid is an aquatic creature with the head and upper body of a female human and the tail of a fish.

claims.statement: Suvannamaccha’s tale involves Hanuman trying to build a stone bridge across the sea.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Suvannamaccha melibatkan Hanuman yang hendak membangun jembatan batu melintasi laut.
claims.quote: one of the heroes, Hanuman attempts to build a bridge of stones across the sea.

claims.statement: The English word mermaid is a compound of "mere" (Old English for sea) and "maid" (a girl or young woman).
claims.statement_id: Kata Inggris "mermaid" adalah gabungan "mere" (bahasa Inggris Kuno untuk laut) dan "maid" (gadis atau perempuan muda).
claims.quote: The English word mermaid is a compound of "mere" (Old English for sea) and "maid" (a girl or young woman).

claims.statement: Mermaids are morally ambiguous creatures, whereas sirens were said to be always malicious and dangerous.
claims.statement_id: Putri duyung adalah makhluk yang secara moral ambigu, sedangkan siren dikatakan selalu jahat dan berbahaya.
claims.quote: While mermaids are morally ambiguous creatures, sirens were said to be always malicious and dangerous

claims.statement: In sailor folklore, mermaids represent both good fortune and disaster.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat pelaut, putri duyung melambangkan keberuntungan sekaligus bencana.
claims.quote: In sailor folklore, mermaids represent both good fortune and disaster.

claims.statement: Mermaids proved popular with sailors as decorations on ships because they were believed to appease the sea, ensuring good weather and a safe way back to land.
claims.statement_id: Putri duyung populer di kalangan pelaut sebagai hiasan haluan kapal karena dipercaya menenangkan laut, menjamin cuaca baik, dan menemukan jalan aman kembali ke daratan.
claims.quote: While many different decorations have been used, mermaids proved popular with the sailors as they were believed to appease the sea, ensuring good weather and finding a safe way back to land.

claims.statement: A famous Greek folktale claimed that Thessalonike, sister of Alexander the Great, was transformed into a mermaid upon her death in 295 BC and lived in the Aegean sea.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah cerita rakyat Yunani menyebut Thessalonike, saudari Alexander Agung, diubah menjadi putri duyung setelah meninggal pada 295 SM dan hidup di Laut Aegea.
claims.quote: A famous Greek folktale claimed that Alexander the Great's sister, Thessalonike was transformed into a mermaid upon her death in 295 BC and lived in the Aegean sea.

claims.statement: Any other answer was said to anger her, and she would conjure a storm and doom the vessel and its sailors to death at sea.
claims.statement_id: Jawaban selain yang benar dikatakan membuatnya marah, dan ia akan memunculkan badai yang membinasakan kapal dan para pelautnya di laut.
claims.quote: Any other answer was said to anger her, and she would conjure a storm and doom the vessel and its sailors to a death at sea.

claims.statement: In West, South and Central Africa, a range of tales exist about mythical water spirits called Mami Wata ("Water as Mother" or "Mother of the Waters").
claims.statement_id: Di Afrika Barat, Selatan, dan Tengah ada berbagai kisah tentang roh air mitos bernama Mami Wata ("Air sebagai Ibu" atau "Ibu Perairan").
claims.quote: In West, South and Central Africa, a range of tales exist about mythical water spirits called Mami Wata (meaning "Water as Mother" or "Mother of the Waters").

claims.statement: The spirit is worshipped for its benevolence in offering beauty, healing and wisdom, and as a way of warding off natural disasters.
claims.statement_id: Roh itu dipuja karena kebaikannya yang memberi kecantikan, penyembuhan, dan kebijaksanaan, serta sebagai cara menangkal bencana alam.
claims.quote: The spirit is worshipped for both their benevolence in offering beauty, healing and wisdom, and as a way of warding off natural disasters.

claims.statement: The Rusalki, water nymphs of Slavic mythology, are often translated as "mermaid"; initially regarded as benevolent spirits of fertility and agriculture, they gained a more sinister description in the 1800s as ghosts of women who died by drowning, luring men and children to their watery graves.
claims.statement_id: Rusalki, nimfa air dalam mitologi Slavia, sering diterjemahkan sebagai "putri duyung"; semula dianggap roh kesuburan dan pertanian yang baik, tetapi pada tahun 1800-an digambarkan lebih jahat, sebagai hantu perempuan yang mati tenggelam dan memikat laki-laki serta anak-anak ke kuburan airnya.
claims.quote: Often translated as "mermaid," the Rusalki are water nymphs of Slavic mythology. While initially regarded as benevolent spirits of fertility and agriculture, Rusalki gained a more sinister description in the 1800s. They were believed to be the ghosts of women who died violent deaths by drowning. In their anger and sorrow, the Rusalki now lured men and children to their watery graves.

claims.statement: Female merrows, with their beauty and long green hair, resemble traditional views of mermaids; their male counterpart is considered grotesque, cruel and more fish than man.
claims.statement_id: Merrow betina, dengan kecantikan dan rambut hijau panjang, menyerupai gambaran tradisional putri duyung; pasangan jantannya dianggap menyeramkan, kejam, dan lebih mirip ikan daripada manusia.
claims.quote: Female merrows, with their beauty and long green hair, resemble our traditional views of mermaids. Their counterpart, the male merrow is considered grotesque, cruel and more fish than man.

claims.statement: The Scottish selkie, often connected to mermaid mythology, lives as a seal in the sea and transforms into a human on land.
claims.statement_id: Selkie Skotlandia, yang sering dikaitkan dengan mitologi putri duyung, hidup sebagai anjing laut di laut dan berubah menjadi manusia di darat.
claims.quote: These shape-shifting creatures live as seals while in the sea and transform into humans while on land.

claims.statement: Melusine is a feminine spirit found in many medieval European folktales who has a serpent or fish's tail and sometimes has wings.
claims.statement_id: Melusine adalah roh perempuan dalam banyak dongeng Eropa abad pertengahan yang berekor ular atau ikan dan kadang bersayap.
claims.quote: A feminine spirit found in many medieval European folktales, the Melusine has a serpent or fish's tail and sometimes has wings.

claims.statement: One of the earliest mermaid legends appeared in Syria around 1000 BC when the goddess Atargatis dove into a lake to take the form of a fish; only her bottom half became a fish, and she kept her top half in human form.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu legenda putri duyung tertua muncul di Suriah sekitar 1000 SM, ketika dewi Atargatis terjun ke danau dan berwujud ikan; hanya bagian bawahnya menjadi ikan, sedangkan bagian atasnya tetap manusia.
claims.quote: One of the earliest mermaid legends appeared in Syria around 1000 BC when the goddess Atargatis dove into a lake to take the form of a fish. As the gods there would not allow her to give up her great beauty, only her bottom half became a fish, and she kept her top half in human form.

claims.statement: The earliest depiction of a mermaid in England can be found in the Norman chapel in Durham Castle, built around 1078 by Saxon stonemasons.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran putri duyung tertua di Inggris ditemukan di kapel Norman di Kastil Durham, yang dibangun sekitar 1078 oleh tukang batu Saxon.
claims.quote: The earliest depiction of a mermaid in England can be found in Norman chapel in Durham Castle, built around 1078 by Saxon stonemasons.

claims.statement: The Havfrue, or Mermaid, is represented in popular tradition sometimes as good, at other times as an evil and treacherous being; she is beautiful in her appearance.
claims.statement_id: Havfrue, atau putri duyung, dalam tradisi rakyat digambarkan kadang sebagai makhluk baik dan kadang sebagai makhluk jahat dan licik; ia cantik rupanya.
claims.quote: The Havfrue, or Mermaid, is represented in the popular tradition sometimes as a good, at other times as an evil and treacherous being. She is beautiful in her appearance.

claims.statement: Fishermen sometimes see her in the bright summer sun, sitting on the surface of the water combing her long golden hair with a golden comb, or driving up her snow-white cattle.
claims.statement_id: Nelayan kadang melihatnya di bawah matahari musim panas, duduk di permukaan air menyisir rambut emas panjangnya dengan sisir emas, atau menggiring ternak putih saljunya.
claims.quote: Fishermen sometimes see her in the bright summer's sun, when a thin mist hangs over the sea, sitting on the surface of the water, and combing her long golden hair with a golden comb, or driving up her snow-white cattle

claims.statement: Her appearance prognosticates both storm and ill success in fishing; drowned people whose bodies are not found are believed to be taken into the dwellings of the Mermaids.
claims.statement_id: Kemunculannya menandakan badai dan kegagalan menangkap ikan; orang yang tenggelam dan jasadnya tidak ditemukan dipercaya dibawa ke tempat tinggal para putri duyung.
claims.quote: Her appearance prognosticates both storm and ill success in their fishing. People that are drowned, and whose bodies are not found, are believed to be taken into the dwellings of the Mermaids.

claims.statement: These beings are also supposed to have the power of foretelling future events; a Mermaid is said to have prophesied the birth of Christian IV of Denmark.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk-makhluk ini dipercaya mampu meramalkan peristiwa masa depan; seorang putri duyung konon meramalkan kelahiran Christian IV dari Denmark.
claims.quote: These beings are also supposed to have the power of foretelling future events. A Mermaid, we are told, prophesied the birth of Christian IV. of Denmark

claims.statement: The Havmand, or Merman, is described as handsome, with green or black hair and beard, dwelling at the bottom of the sea or in cliffs and hills near the shore, and is regarded as a rather good and beneficent kind of being.
claims.statement_id: Havmand, atau manusia duyung, digambarkan berbentuk tampan dengan rambut dan janggut hijau atau hitam, tinggal di dasar laut atau di tebing dan bukit dekat pantai, dan dianggap makhluk yang cukup baik dan murah hati.
claims.quote: The Havmand, or Merman, is described as of a handsome form, with green or black hair and beard. He dwells either in the bottom of the sea, or in the cliffs and hills near the sea shore, and is regarded as rather a good and beneficent kind of being

claims.statement: In the Shetland tale "The Mermaid Wife," a man saw sea-people dancing on the sand with seal-skins lying near them; they hurried to put on their garments and plunged into the sea in the form of seals.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah "The Mermaid Wife" dari Shetland, seorang laki-laki melihat penghuni laut menari di pasir dengan kulit anjing laut tergeletak di dekat mereka; mereka bergegas memakai kulit itu dan terjun ke laut dalam wujud anjing laut.
claims.quote: Near them he saw lying on the ground several seal-skins. As the man approached the dancers, all gave over their merriment, and flew like lightning to secure their garments; then clothing themselves, plunged in the form of seals into the sea.

claims.statement: Without her seal-skin robe, the sea-maiden could not rejoin her family and friends below the waters and must remain an unwilling inhabitant of the region enlightened by the sun.
claims.statement_id: Tanpa kulit anjing lautnya, perempuan laut itu tidak dapat bergabung kembali dengan keluarganya di bawah air dan harus tetap tinggal di daratan.
claims.quote: she never could hope to rejoin her family and friends below the waters, but must remain an unwilling inhabitant of the region enlightened by the sun.

claims.statement: After recovering her skin, the wife took the form of a seal and plunged into the sea.
claims.statement_id: Setelah mendapatkan kembali kulitnya, sang istri berubah menjadi anjing laut dan terjun ke laut.
claims.quote: But he only arrived in time to see his wife take the form of a seal, and from the ledge of a rock plunge into the sea.

claims.statement: The Lady of Gollerus of Ireland resembles the Mermaid-wife stories; instead of an entire dress it is a cap, named Cohuleen Driuth, without which she cannot return to her subaqueous abode.
claims.statement_id: Nyonya Gollerus dari Irlandia menyerupai kisah istri putri duyung; alih-alih pakaian utuh, ia memiliki topi bernama Cohuleen Driuth, yang tanpanya ia tidak dapat kembali ke tempat tinggalnya di bawah air.
claims.quote: Thus the Lady of Gollerus resembles the Mermaid-wife and others which we have already related. Instead, however, of an entire dress, it is a kind of cap, named Cohuleen Driuth, without which she cannot return to her subaqueous abode.

claims.statement: Mermaid stories are found from coastal settlements in Ireland to the landlocked Karoo desert in South Africa.
claims.statement_id: Kisah putri duyung ditemukan dari permukiman pesisir di Irlandia hingga gurun Karoo di Afrika Selatan yang tidak berpantai.
claims.quote: from coastal settlements in Ireland to the landlocked Karoo desert in South Africa

claims.statement: At other times she comes as a beautiful maiden, chilled and shivering with the cold of the night, to the fires the fishers have kindled, hoping to entice them to her love.
claims.statement_id: Di lain waktu ia datang sebagai gadis cantik yang menggigil kedinginan ke api yang dinyalakan nelayan, berharap memikat mereka agar mencintainya.
claims.quote: At other times she comes as a beautiful maiden, chilled and shivering with the cold of the night, to the fires the fishers have kindled, hoping by this means to entice them to her love.

claims.statement: It is a strange carving, with the mermaid found alongside two leopards and several hunting scenes.
claims.statement_id: Ukiran itu aneh: putri duyung ditemukan bersama dua macan tutul dan beberapa adegan berburu.
claims.quote: It is a strange carving, with the mermaid found alongside two leopards and several hunting scenes.

claims.statement: Many ancient Greek myths equate sirens with mermaids; although they share many characteristics, they are now seen as two different entities.
claims.statement_id: Banyak mitos Yunani kuno menyamakan siren dengan putri duyung; walau banyak kesamaan, keduanya kini dipandang sebagai dua makhluk berbeda.
claims.quote: Many ancient Greek myths equate sirens with mermaids. However, while they share many characteristics, they are now seen as two different entities.

claims.statement: Hephaestus is a Greek god of fire and metal crafts.
claims.statement_id: Hephaestus adalah dewa Yunani bagi api dan kerajinan logam.
claims.quote: is the Greek god of artisans, blacksmiths, carpenters, craftsmen, fire, metallurgy, metalworking, sculpture, and volcanoes.

claims.statement: Hephaestus is shown as a bearded man with hammer and tongs.
claims.statement_id: Hephaestus digambarkan sebagai lelaki berjanggut dengan palu dan penjepit logam.
claims.quote: He was depicted as a bearded man holding a hammer and tongs--the tools of a smith--and sometimes riding a donkey.

claims.statement: Hephaestus made armor for Achilles at Thetis's request.
claims.statement_id: Hephaestus membuat zirah Achilles atas permintaan Thetis.
claims.quote: The crafting of the armour of Akhilleus (Achilles) at the request of the hero's mother Thetis.

claims.statement: In a Homeric version Hephaestus is a son of Zeus and Hera.
claims.statement_id: Versi Homer menyebut Hephaestus putra Zeus dan Hera.
claims.quote: the god of fire, was, according to the Homeric account, the son of Zeus and Hera.

claims.statement: Other traditions say Hera bore Hephaestus without a father.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain menyatakan Hera melahirkan Hephaestus tanpa ayah.
claims.quote: Later traditions state that he had no father, and that Hera gave birth to him independent of Zeus

claims.statement: Hephaestus trapped Hera in a cursed throne.
claims.statement_id: Hephaestus menjebak Hera dalam singgasana terkutuk.
claims.quote: The capture of Hera in a cursed throne and his return to Olympos.

claims.statement: Romans equated Hephaestus with Vulcan.
claims.statement_id: Bangsa Romawi menyamakan Hephaestus dengan Vulcan.
claims.quote: In Rome, he was equated with Vulcan.

claims.statement: Hephaestus was especially worshipped at Athens and Lemnos.
claims.statement_id: Hephaestus terutama dipuja di Athena dan Lemnos.
claims.quote: Hephaistos was particularly worshipped at Athens and Lemnos in the northeast Aegean.

claims.statement: Hephaestus forged objects for Olympian gods.
claims.statement_id: Hephaestus menempa berbagai benda untuk dewa Olimpus.
claims.quote: He was the brilliant blacksmith of the Olympian gods, for whom he fashioned magnificent houses, armour, and ingenious devices.

claims.statement: Hephaistos was the Olympian god of fire, smiths, craftsmen, metalworking, stonemasonry and sculpture.
claims.statement_id: Hephaistos adalah dewa Olimpus untuk api, pandai besi, pengrajin, pengerjaan logam, pemahatan batu, dan seni patung.
claims.quote: HEPHAISTOS (Hephaestus) was the Olympian god of fire, smiths, craftsmen, metalworking, stonemasonry and sculpture.

claims.statement: Hephaestus is the god of fire, especially as a power of nature in volcanic districts and as the indispensable means in arts and manufactures.
claims.statement_id: Hephaestus adalah dewa api, terutama sebagai kekuatan alam di daerah vulkanik dan sebagai sarana yang tak tergantikan dalam seni dan kerajinan.
claims.quote: Hephaestus is the god of fire, especially in so far as it manifests itself as a power of physical nature in volcanic districts, and in so far as it is the indispensable means in arts and manufactures

claims.statement: One of his famous myths is his fall from Olympos, in which he was cast away by Hera at birth.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu kisah terkenalnya adalah jatuhnya dari Olimpus ketika Hera membuangnya saat lahir.
claims.quote: His fall from Olympos in which he was cast away by Hera at birth.

claims.statement: The story of the adultery of his wife Aphrodite, who was trapped with Ares in a golden net.
claims.statement_id: Kisah perselingkuhan istrinya, Aphrodite, yang terperangkap bersama Ares dalam jaring emas.
claims.quote: The adultery of his wife Aphrodite who was trapped with Ares in a golden net.

claims.statement: Hephaistos crafted Pandora, the first woman, at the command of Zeus.
claims.statement_id: Hephaistos membuat Pandora, perempuan pertama, atas perintah Zeus.
claims.quote: The crafting of Pandora, the first woman, at the command of Zeus.

claims.statement: He crafted the cursed necklace of Harmonia which doomed her descendants to a cycle of tragedy.
claims.statement_id: Ia membuat kalung terkutuk Harmonia yang menjerumuskan keturunannya ke dalam rangkaian tragedi.
claims.quote: The crafting of the cursed necklace of Harmonia which doomed her descendants to a cycle of tragedy.

claims.statement: In the Trojan War he fought the river-god Skamandros (Scamander) with fire.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Perang Troya ia melawan dewa sungai Skamandros (Scamander) dengan api.
claims.quote: The Trojan War in which he fought the river-god Skamandros (Scamander) with fire.

claims.statement: Zeus seized him by the leg and hurled him down from Olympus; Hephaestus was a whole day falling and came down on the island of Lemnos, where he was kindly received by the Sintians.
claims.statement_id: Zeus menyambar kakinya dan melemparkannya dari Olimpus; Hephaestus jatuh sehari penuh dan mendarat di pulau Lemnos, tempat suku Sintian menyambutnya dengan ramah.
claims.quote: he seized him by the leg, and hulled him down from Olympus. Hephaestus was a whole day falling, but in the evening he came down in the island of Lemnos, where he was kindly received by the Sintians.

claims.statement: The marine divinities Thetis and Eurynome received him, and he dwelt with them for nine years in a grotto, surrounded by Oceanus, making them a variety of ornaments.
claims.statement_id: Dewi laut Thetis dan Eurynome menerimanya, dan ia tinggal bersama mereka selama sembilan tahun di sebuah gua, dikelilingi Oceanus, membuatkan berbagai perhiasan bagi mereka.
claims.quote: But the marine divinities, Thetis and Eurynome, received him, and he dwelt with them for nine years in a grotto, surrounded by Oceanus, making for them a variety of ornaments.

claims.statement: In Olympus, Hephaestus had his own palace, imperishable and shining like stars, containing his workshop with the anvil and twenty bellows which worked spontaneously at his bidding.
claims.statement_id: Di Olimpus, Hephaestus memiliki istana sendiri yang abadi dan berkilau seperti bintang, berisi bengkel dengan landasan dan dua puluh alat tiup yang bekerja sendiri atas perintahnya.
claims.quote: In Olympus, Hephaestus had his own palace, imperishable and shining like stars: it contained his workshop, with the anvil, and twenty bellows, which worked spontaneously at his bidding.

claims.statement: In later accounts the Cyclopes (Brontes, Steropes, Pyracmon, and others) are his workmen and servants, and his workshop is no longer in Olympus but in the interior of some volcanic isle.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah yang lebih belakangan, para Cyclops (Brontes, Steropes, Pyracmon, dan lainnya) adalah pekerja dan pelayannya, dan bengkelnya tidak lagi di Olimpus melainkan di dalam sebuah pulau vulkanik.
claims.quote: In later accounts, the Cyclopes, Brontes, Steropes, Pyracmon, and others, are his workmen and servants, and his workshop is no longer represented as in Olympus, but in the interior of some volcanic isle.

claims.statement: The wife of Hephaestus also lived in his palace: in the Iliad she is called a Charis, in the Odyssey Aphrodite, and in Hesiod's Theogony she is named Aglaia.
claims.statement_id: Istri Hephaestus tinggal di istananya: dalam Iliad ia disebut seorang Charis, dalam Odyssey Aphrodite, dan dalam Theogony karya Hesiod ia bernama Aglaia.
claims.quote: The wife of Hephaestus also lived in his palace: in the Iliad she is called a Charis, in the Odyssey Aphrodite ... and in Hesiod's Theogony (945) she is named Aglaia.

claims.statement: Later writers describe his lameness as the consequence of his second fall, while Homer makes him lame and weak from his birth.
claims.statement_id: Penulis yang lebih belakangan menggambarkan kepincangannya sebagai akibat jatuhnya yang kedua, sedangkan Homeros menjadikannya lumpuh dan lemah sejak lahir.
claims.quote: Later writers describe his lameness as the consequence of his second fall, while Homer makes him lame and weak from his birth.

claims.statement: Lemnian earth from the spot where Hephaestus had fallen was believed to cure madness, the bites of snakes, and haemorrhage.
claims.statement_id: Tanah Lemnos dari tempat Hephaestus jatuh dipercaya dapat menyembuhkan kegilaan, gigitan ular, dan pendarahan.
claims.quote: Lemnian earth (terra Lemnia) from the spot on which Hephaestus had fallen was believed to cure madness, the bites of snakes, and haemorrhage

claims.statement: Like Athena, he gives skill to mortal artists and, together with her, was believed to have taught men the arts which embellish and adorn life.
claims.statement_id: Bersama Athena, Hephaestus dipercaya memberi keterampilan kepada seniman fana dan mengajarkan manusia seni-seni yang memperindah kehidupan.
claims.quote: for, like her, he give skill to mortal artists, and, conjointly with her, he was believed to have taught men the arts which embellish and adorn life.

claims.statement: According to Homeric Hymn 20, with Athene he taught men glorious crafts throughout the world; now that they have learned crafts through Hephaistos, they live a peaceful life in their own houses the whole year round.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Himne Homerik 20, bersama Athene ia mengajarkan manusia kerajinan yang mulia; kini setelah belajar dari Hephaistos, manusia hidup damai di rumah sendiri sepanjang tahun.
claims.quote: With bright-eyed Athene he taught men glorious crafts throughout the world ... But now that they have learned crafts through Hephaistos the famed worker (klytotekhnes), easily they live a peaceful life in their own houses the whole year round.

claims.statement: During the best period of Greek art he was represented as a vigorous bearded man, characterised by his hammer or some other instrument, his oval cap, and the chiton leaving the right shoulder and arm uncovered.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa terbaik seni Yunani, ia digambarkan sebagai lelaki kekar berjanggut, dengan palu atau alat lain, topi oval, dan chiton yang membuka bahu dan lengan kanan.
claims.quote: During the best period of Grecian art, he was represented as a vigorous man with a beard, and is characterised by his hammer or some other instrument, his oval cap, and the chiton, which leaves the right shoulder and arm uncovered.

claims.statement: The Greeks frequently placed small dwarf-like statues of the god near the hearth.
claims.statement_id: Orang Yunani sering menaruh patung kecil mirip kurcaci sang dewa di dekat perapian.
claims.quote: The Greeks frequently placed small dwarf-like statues of the god near the hearth

claims.statement: Hephaistos is credited with making the sceptre and aegis of Zeus, the helmet of Hermes, secret locking doors for Hera's chambers, and Pandora, the first woman, whom he sculpted out of clay.
claims.statement_id: Hephaistos dikreditkan membuat tongkat kerajaan dan aegis Zeus, helm Hermes, pintu terkunci rahasia untuk kamar Hera, dan Pandora, perempuan pertama yang ia bentuk dari tanah liat.
claims.quote: As an ingenious craftsman, Hephaistos is credited with making the sceptre and aegis of Zeus, the helmet of Hermes, secret locking doors for Hera's chambers, and even the lovely first woman, Pandora, who he sculpted out of clay.

claims.statement: He also manufactured automatons: gold maids who could speak and were intelligent for himself, bronze Talos as a gift for King Minos of Crete, and watchdogs for Alcinous, king of Phaeacia.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga membuat automaton: pelayan emas yang dapat berbicara dan cerdas untuk dirinya, Talos perunggu sebagai hadiah bagi Raja Minos dari Kreta, dan anjing penjaga bagi Alcinous, raja Phaeacia.
claims.quote: He also manufactured automatons - gold maids who could speak and were intelligent - for himself, bronze Talos as a gift for King Minos of Crete, and watchdogs for Alcinous, king of Phaeacia.

claims.statement: Hephaistos had his workshop beneath volcanoes such as Mount Etna on Sicily.
claims.statement_id: Hephaistos memiliki bengkel di bawah gunung berapi seperti Gunung Etna di Sisilia.
claims.quote: Hephaistos had his workshop beneath volcanos such as Mount Etna on Sicily.

claims.statement: The god had a lame foot and so was unique as the only less-than-perfect god.
claims.statement_id: Sang dewa berkaki pincang sehingga unik sebagai satu-satunya dewa yang kurang sempurna.
claims.quote: The god had a lame foot and so he was unique as the only less-than-perfect god.

claims.statement: He is said to have been thrown from the heavens by his mother (or in other accounts by Zeus) because of his ugliness, and on landing on the island of Lemnos the god was crippled.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan dilempar dari langit oleh ibunya (atau menurut kisah lain oleh Zeus) karena kejelekannya, dan setelah mendarat di pulau Lemnos, sang dewa menjadi pincang.
claims.quote: he is said to have been thrown from the heavens by his mother (or in other accounts by Zeus) because of his ugliness and on landing on the island of Lemnos, the god was crippled.

claims.statement: Hephaistos married Aphrodite; the union occurred because he captured his mother Hera in the invisible chains of a throne he had built, and the wedding was the price of release.
claims.statement_id: Hephaistos menikahi Aphrodite; persatuan itu terjadi karena ia menjebak ibunya, Hera, dalam rantai tak terlihat pada singgasana buatannya, dan pernikahan itu menjadi harga pembebasan.
claims.quote: Hephaistos married the goddess Aphrodite. The unlikely union occurred as a result of Hephaistos capturing his mother Hera in the invisible chains of a throne he had built, and the wedding was the price of release.

claims.statement: The scene is popular in Greek art and usually shows Dionysos leading Hephaistos, under the influence of wine, back to Olympus to free the entrapped Hera.
claims.statement_id: Adegan itu populer dalam seni Yunani dan biasanya menggambarkan Dionysos menuntun Hephaistos yang mabuk anggur kembali ke Olimpus untuk membebaskan Hera yang terjerat.
claims.quote: The scene is a popular one in Greek art and usually depicts Dionysos leading Hephaistos, under the influence of wine, back to Olympus to free the entrapped Hera.

claims.statement: The god even acted as midwife at the birth of Athena, splitting Zeus' head with his axe so that the goddess might be born from there.
claims.statement_id: Sang dewa bahkan menjadi bidan saat kelahiran Athena dengan membelah kepala Zeus dengan kapaknya agar sang dewi lahir dari sana.
claims.quote: The god even acted as midwife at the birth of Athena, splitting Zeus' head with his axe so that the goddess might be born from there.

claims.statement: Supporting the Achaeans in the Trojan War, he fights and defeats the river god Xanthos with fire and produces a shield of bronze, gold, silver, and tin for Achilles.
claims.statement_id: Mendukung bangsa Akhaia dalam Perang Troya, ia mengalahkan dewa sungai Xanthos dengan api dan membuat perisai dari perunggu, emas, perak, dan timah bagi Achilles.
claims.quote: Supporting the Achaeans in the Trojan War, he memorably fights and defeats the river god Xanthos with fire and produces magnificent armour and a shield of bronze, gold, silver, and tin for Achilles

claims.statement: Hephaistos' most notable offspring in Greek mythology were Erechtheus, the first king of Athens, and Periphetes, who lived near Epidaurus and famously killed passing strangers with an iron club.
claims.statement_id: Keturunan Hephaistos yang paling terkenal dalam mitologi Yunani adalah Erechtheus, raja pertama Athena, dan Periphetes, yang tinggal dekat Epidaurus dan terkenal membunuh orang asing yang lewat dengan gada besi.
claims.quote: Hephaistos' most notable offspring in Greek mythology were Erechtheus, the first king of Athens, and Periphetes, who lived near Epidaurus and famously killed passing strangers with an iron club.

claims.statement: The Doric temple built c. 449 BCE, sometimes known as the Hephaisteion or Thesium, was jointly dedicated to the god and Athena in Athens.
claims.statement_id: Kuil Doric yang dibangun sekitar 449 SM, kadang disebut Hephaisteion atau Thesium, didedikasikan bersama bagi sang dewa dan Athena di Athena.
claims.quote: The Doric temple built c. 449 BCE and sometimes known as the Hephaisteion or Thesium

claims.statement: According to Sophocles, blacksmiths would march through the city carrying their tools during the annual Chalkeia festival which honoured the pair of gods.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Sophocles, para pandai besi berarak melewati kota membawa perkakas mereka pada festival tahunan Chalkeia yang menghormati sepasang dewa itu.
claims.quote: blacksmiths would march through the city carrying their tools during the annual Chalkeia festival which honoured the pair of gods.

claims.statement: On Lemnos, Hephaistos gave his name to the city of Hephaistia, which had a sanctuary dedicated to him.
claims.statement_id: Di Lemnos, Hephaistos memberi namanya kepada kota Hephaistia, yang memiliki tempat suci untuknya.
claims.quote: Hephaistos gave his name to the city of Hephaistia, which had a sanctuary dedicated to him.

claims.statement: In ancient Greek art, Hephaistos is often depicted wearing a pilos or workman's hat and an exomis or workman's tunic, holding tongs, an axe, hammer, saw, or chisel, and frequently riding a mule side-saddle.
claims.statement_id: Dalam seni Yunani kuno, Hephaistos sering digambarkan memakai pilos (topi pekerja) dan exomis (tunik pekerja), memegang penjepit, kapak, palu, gergaji, atau pahat, dan sering menunggang bagal dengan duduk menyamping.
claims.quote: In ancient Greek art, Hephaistos is often depicted wearing a pilos or workman's hat and an exomis or workman's tunic. He also often holds tongs, an axe, hammer, saw, or chisel, and is frequently seen riding a mule side-saddle.

claims.statement: The origins of Hephaistos are obscure, but he probably derives from the common idea that early kings should also be masters of certain crafts, especially metalwork, and perhaps magic (which would have included the manipulation of fire).
claims.statement_id: Asal-usul Hephaistos tidak jelas, tetapi ia mungkin berasal dari gagasan umum bahwa raja-raja awal juga harus menguasai kerajinan tertentu, terutama pengerjaan logam, dan mungkin sihir (yang mencakup pengolahan api).
claims.quote: The origins of Hephaistos are obscure but he probably derives from the common idea that early kings should also be masters at certain crafts, especially metalwork, and perhaps, too, magic (which would have included the manipulation of fire).

claims.statement: Both Homer and Hesiod describe Hephaistos as "the cripple-foot god" and "the lame one".
claims.statement_id: Homeros dan Hesiod sama-sama menyebut Hephaistos "dewa berkaki pincang" dan "si pincang".
claims.quote: Both Homer and Hesiod describe Hephaistos as 'the cripple-foot god' and 'the lame one'.

claims.statement: The god's physical problems may have been a reflection in myth of the reality of a blacksmith's harsh working conditions, where repeated hammering and toxic fumes can take their toll on both mind and body.
claims.statement_id: Masalah fisik sang dewa mungkin merupakan cerminan dalam mitos dari kerasnya kondisi kerja pandai besi, tempat pemukulan berulang dan asap beracun dapat merusak pikiran dan tubuh.
claims.quote: The god's physical problems may have been a reflection in myth of the reality of a blacksmith's harsh working conditions where repeated hammering and toxic fumes can take their toll on both mind and body.

claims.statement: In the Iliad, the house of Hephaestus is imperishable, decked with stars, and wrought all of bronze, built by the crook-foot god himself.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Iliad, rumah Hephaestus abadi, bertabur bintang, dan seluruhnya dari perunggu, dibangun sendiri oleh dewa berkaki bengkok itu.
claims.quote: came unto the house of Hephaestus, imperishable, decked with stars, preeminent among the houses of immortals, wrought all of bronze, that the crook-foot god himself had built him.

claims.statement: In the Iliad, Hephaestus was fashioning twenty tripods for the wall of his hall, each set on golden wheels so that of themselves they might enter the gathering of the gods at his wish and return to his house.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Iliad, Hephaestus membuat dua puluh tripod untuk dinding aulanya, masing-masing berroda emas sehingga dapat masuk sendiri ke pertemuan para dewa atas kehendaknya lalu kembali ke rumahnya.
claims.quote: he was fashioning tripods, twenty in all, to stand around the wall of his well-builded hall, and golden wheels had he set beneath the base of each that of themselves they might enter the gathering of the gods at his wish and again return to his house, a wonder to behold.

claims.statement: In the Iliad, handmaidens wrought of gold in the semblance of living maids moved to support their lord; in them is understanding in their hearts, and speech and strength.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Iliad, pelayan perempuan dari emas yang menyerupai gadis hidup bergerak menopang tuan mereka; mereka punya pengertian di hati serta bicara dan tenaga.
claims.quote: there moved swiftly to support their lord handmaidens wrought of gold in the semblance of living maids. In them is understanding in their hearts, and in them speech and strength

claims.statement: In the Iliad, Hephaestus says Thetis saved him after he had fallen afar through the will of his shameless mother, who was fain to hide him away by reason of his lameness.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Iliad, Hephaestus berkata Thetis menyelamatkannya setelah ia jatuh jauh atas kehendak ibunya yang tak tahu malu, yang ingin menyembunyikannya karena kepincangannya.
claims.quote: even she that saved me when pain was come upon me after I had fallen afar through the will of my shameless mother, that was fain to hide me away by reason of my lameness.

claims.statement: In the Iliad, the twenty bellows blew upon the melting-vats, sending forth a ready blast, serving Hephaestus as he wished while his work went on.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Iliad, dua puluh alat tiup meniupkan hembusan ke bejana peleburan, melayani Hephaestus sesuai kehendaknya selagi ia bekerja.
claims.quote: And the bellows, twenty in all, blew upon the melting-vats, sending forth a ready blast of every force, now to further him as he laboured hard, and again in whatsoever way Hephaestus might wish and his work go on.

claims.statement: In the Iliad, Hephaestus first fashioned a great and sturdy shield adorned cunningly in every part, with five layers and many curious devices.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Iliad, Hephaestus pertama-tama membuat perisai besar dan kokoh yang dihias dengan cerdik di setiap bagiannya, dengan lima lapisan dan banyak hiasan yang unik.
claims.quote: First fashioned he a shield, great and sturdy, adorning it cunningly in every part, and round about it set a bright rim, threefold and glittering, and therefrom made fast a silver baldric. Five were the layers of the shield itself; and on it he wrought many curious devices with cunning skill.

claims.statement: In the Iliad, on the shield Hephaestus wrought the earth, the heavens, the sea, the unwearied sun, and the moon at the full.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Iliad, pada perisai itu Hephaestus menempa bumi, langit, laut, matahari yang tak kenal lelah, dan bulan purnama.
claims.quote: Therein he wrought the earth, therein the heavens therein the sea, and the unwearied sun, and the moon at the full
